answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a ferrous as the anchor of the cost.
